name: Egg Hunt
label: Dischord
lede: In the spring of 1986 Ian MacKaye and Jeff Nelson flew to London for a distribution meeting and spent Easter weekend in a garage studio in Wood Green. Four songs later, the two Minor Threat founders had made the last music they would ever record together.

eras.title: Easter in Wood Green
eras.text: Embrace had broken up and Minor Threat was two and a half years gone. MacKaye and Nelson, who ran Dischord, crossed the Atlantic on label business, and a stop at Southern Records turned into Dischord's twentieth release.

years.h: Dischord's founders fly to London for a distribution meeting
years.p: MacKaye and Nelson go to England to talk European distribution, per Wikipedia. [[John Loder|39baeee6-dc33-470e-a62d-099c89463590]], who runs Southern Records, offers them studio time while they're in town.

years.h: Me and You had been a basement song for years
years.p: Dischord says MacKaye and Nelson had played it together in a basement for years, since the [[Teen Idles|84e8d8bf-da21-4488-89e5-50a4c12ff4fa]] in 1979. In London it finally goes on tape.

years.src: Wikipedia: Me and You (Egg Hunt song) · Wikipedia: Egg Hunt
years.h: Embrace said no to We All Fall Down, so Egg Hunt took it
years.p: MacKaye wrote the song for [[Embrace|9d1ad8e3-8740-429a-bdc5-52f96a9c4431]] and the band turned it down. It becomes the B-side of the London single.
years.xp:
AllMusic's Jack Rabid, as Wikipedia quotes him, called it a "post-punk melodic masterpiece" and heard in it a reflection on Washington's 1985 Revolution Summer.

Wikipedia lists it at 2:48 or 2:49 depending on the page, against 3:48 for Me and You: a 6:37 single, near enough.

years.h: Egg Hunt tries to become a band, and doesn't
years.p: Back in D.C., MacKaye and Nelson try it with [[Gray Matter|c9065214-ba09-4c2c-b341-35713b702264]]'s [[Geoff Turner|591fc466-2668-4524-852d-a6cc5f18cff7]] and [[Steve Niles|ce17b293-3129-426d-b9d3-7403dfda4d8f]]. In Dischord's words it wasn't meant to be: MacKaye leaves, and the other three become Three.

years.h: 2 Songs comes out in October as Dischord No. 20
years.p: Two of the four songs recorded at Southern make the single. Dischord calls the session the last time MacKaye and Nelson recorded together.
years.xp:
Southern ran out of a row house in Wood Green with a 24-track studio in the garage. Wikipedia gives the session dates as March 27, 28 and 30, with Loder engineering. Easter Sunday fell on March 30, which is where the name came from.

MacKaye sings and plays guitar and bass, his recording debut as a guitarist per Wikipedia. Nelson plays drums and, in Dischord's credits, gum. Wikipedia prints MacKaye saying they "decided to fuck around in the studio"; Dischord says they had such a good time they decided to release a single to mark it.

Only two of the four songs came out. The partnership that built the Teen Idles, [[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]] and Dischord itself ends on record with a holiday single.

eras.title: Two roads out of the garage
eras.text: Egg Hunt never became a band. MacKaye and Nelson kept running Dischord together and made their music apart.

years.p: Fugazi plays its first show that September, with MacKaye on vocals and guitar, the instrument he first recorded on in Wood Green.

years.h: Nelson drums for Three, which splits before its album
years.p: Three grew out of the Egg Hunt tryouts. Dark Days Coming comes out on Dischord after the band has already broken up.

eras.title: A holiday single that keeps coming back
eras.text: Dischord kept 2 Songs in print, on CD, on a box set and on colored vinyl, and kept finding people who had never heard of Egg Hunt.

years.p: Wikipedia dates the CD reissue of the Egg Hunt single to June 16.

years.h: Me and You turns up on 20 Years of Dischord
years.p: The A-side is one of the tracks on Dischord's anniversary box set, catalog No. 125.
Dischord reissues the Egg Hunt 7-inch on light blue vinyl, per Wikipedia.
